diagnostic_evidence.quote: Define $c = \frac{2}{a+b}$. Then, the image of the scaled function $cf$ on $[\ell,u]$ is $[ca,cb]$ and $cf$ satisfies

issues.failure_explanation: The induction step bounds the error of an arbitrary competitor $\widetilde p_T \circ f$ through the ratio $a/b$ of the competitor's image $[a,b]$, the scaling $c=2/(a+b)$, and a rescaling to $[a/b,1]$; all of these steps require $0 < a \le b$. For competitors with nonpositive image the claimed ratio bound is actually false (e.g. $f=-p_1$ has image $[-u_2,-\ell_2]$ with ratio $u_2/\ell_2 \approx 240 \gg \ell_2/u_2$), the formula $\max\{|1-ca|,|cb-1|\}=(b-a)/(a+b)$ can yield a negative value, and the rescaled interval $[a/b,1]$ is degenerate. The theorem's statement remains true (for $b<0$ one applies the established ratio bound to the valid composition $-f$ and uses oddness to get error $\ge \min_p\max_{[-b,-a]}|1-p| \ge 1-\ell_{T+1}$; for $b=0$ the error is trivially $\ge 1$ since $\widetilde p_T(0)=0$), but this case is missing from the proof.

failure_location.quote: Let the image of $f$ on $[\ell,u]$ be $[a,b]$. We will prove that $\frac{a}{b} \leq \frac{\ell_T}{u_T}$  by contradiction.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the degenerate case to the induction: if $b=0$ the competitor's error is at least $1$; if $b<0$, apply the positive-image ratio bound to the valid composition $-f$ (negate the outermost factor) to obtain $(-a)/(-b) \le \ell_T/u_T$, and conclude via oddness that the competitor's error is at least $\min_p\max_{[-b,-a]}|1-p| \ge 1-\ell_{T+1}$. No statement changes.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the paper's central worst-case optimality theorem is incomplete as written for competitor compositions whose image lies in $(-\infty,0]$. The theorem's statement, the optimal error value $1-\ell_{T+1}$, and its downstream use in theorem:convergence are unaffected because the missing case admits a short separate argument.
issues.title: Greedy optimality proof's competitor analysis breaks down for nonpositive images
issues.why_classification: The omitted case is degenerate and the repair is a short symmetry argument reusing the induction hypothesis; the theorem's statement, the $1-\ell_{T+1}$ error value, and all downstream guarantees survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose $x = \ell$ was a minimum of $e(x)$ on $[\ell,u]$.
First note that $p^{\star}$ is trivially non-negative on $[\ell,u]$, or else $p(x) = 0$ would be a better polynomial.
We must also have $e'(\ell) \geq 0$ or else $x=\ell$ is not a minimum of $e(x)$.

issues.failure_explanation: To rule out $x=\ell$ being a minimum of $e=1-p^*$ the proof needs a point $\delta \in [0,\ell]$ with $p^{*'}(\delta)>0$ (so that $e'(\delta)<0$, and the IVT together with $e'(\ell)\ge0$ yields a stationary point in $(0,\ell)$, contradicting Step 1). The stated justification ("or else the zero polynomial $p(x)=0$ would be a better approximation") does not imply this, since the zero polynomial has error exactly $1$ while the optimal error is $<1$. The correct argument is: under the supposition $e(\ell)=-E$ one has $p^*(\ell)=1+E>0=p^*(0)$; if $p^{*'}$ were nonpositive on all of $[0,\ell]$ then $p^*(\ell)\le0$, a contradiction, so such a $\delta$ exists and the IVT argument goes through. The lemma's conclusion is correct, but the written proof does not establish it.

failure_location.quote: Hence, since $p^{\star}(0) = 0$ we must have ${p^{*}}'(\delta) > 0$ for some $\delta \in [0,\ell]$, or else the zero polynomial $p(x) = 0$ would be a better approximation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the mean-value/IVT argument: under the supposition $e(\ell)=-E$ one has $p^*(\ell)=1+E>0=p^*(0)$; if $p^{*'}$ were nonpositive on $[0,\ell]$ then $p^*(\ell)\le0$, contradicting this, so $p^{*'}(\delta)>0$ for some $\delta\in(0,\ell)$; then $e'(\delta)<0$ together with $e'_+(\ell)\ge0$ forces a stationary point of $e$ in $(0,\ell)$, contradicting Step 1. No statement or guarantee changes.
issues.overall_effect: The key identity of the base-case lemma ($p^*(\ell)=\min_{[\ell,u]}p^*$, hence the identities in eq:newbounds) rests on an unjustified step. theorem:greedy cites this lemma both for eq:newbounds and for the $T=1$ base case, so its proof is incomplete until the argument is supplied; all statements are true and locally repairable.
issues.title: Base-case lemma for the greedy theorem uses an unjustified inference
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is correct and the missing step is a short standard MVT/IVT argument; every substantive claim and guarantee survives with a local proof repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, when $\ell/u \geq 1-\epsilon_d^{1/3}$, where $\epsilon_{\text{double}} \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-16}$ is the double precision machine epsilon, then $|p^{\star}(x) - p(x)| \leq 2 \epsilon_{\text{double}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For $p(x)=\tilde p(x/u)$ with $\tilde p(y)=(15y-10y^3+3y^5)/8$, the exact error is $1-\tilde p(y)=\frac{(1-y)^3(3y^2+9y+8)}{8}$, so $\max_{x\in[\ell,u]}|1-p(x)|=\frac{(1-\ell/u)^3(3(\ell/u)^2+9(\ell/u)+8)}{8}$, which strictly exceeds $(1-\ell/u)^3$ (e.g. at $\ell/u=1/2$ the true maximum is $0.2070>0.125$). The last displayed inequality is therefore false; the Kenney-Laub bound used in the convergence proof gives $(1-\ell^2/u^2)^3$ instead. The consequent estimate $|p^*-p|\le 2\epsilon_{\text{double}}$ for $\ell/u\ge 1-\epsilon_{\text{double}}^{1/3}$ should carry a larger constant ($5\epsilon_{\text{double}}$), but the early-return threshold and the algorithm are unaffected in practice.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $(1-\ell/u)^3$ by $(1-\ell^2/u^2)^3$ (equivalently the exact expression $\frac{(1-\ell/u)^3(3(\ell/u)^2+9(\ell/u)+8)}{8}$) in the display and adjust the constant in the following sentence to $5\epsilon_{\text{double}}$; the threshold $\ell/u \ge 1-\epsilon_{\text{double}}^{1/3}$ remains valid up to the constant factor.
issues.overall_effect: A displayed bound in the Remez section is false as stated, but only by a constant factor; the heuristic threshold for returning the Pade polynomial, the Remez algorithm, and every theorem are unaffected.
issues.title: False displayed bound for the degree-5 Pade polynomial's error in the Remez section
issues.why_classification: The inequality is false but only by a constant factor; the repair is a local bound correction and every conclusion that depends on it (the early-return threshold) survives unchanged.
